name: Meridian Ledger

stars.name: Ledger
stars.notes: An ancient, metronomic orange dwarf; its light has barely flickered since before most younger stars in the Shelf were born, which is why the Guild trusts its observations.

planets.name: Kiln
planets.notes: A crack-glazed cinder hugging the star; lander pilots use its shadowline to calibrate heat shields, and little else goes near it.

planets.name: Tideledger
planets.notes: Warm shallow seas under long orange days; the fisher-clans who settled here keep tidal almanacs so precise that half the sector sets its clocks by them. Population roughly four hundred thousand.

planets.name: Scrivener
planets.notes: Thin-aired highlands dotted with the stone foundations of the first failed colony; waystation crews camp among them and leave offerings at the old wellhead.

planets.name: Foliobank
planets.notes: A dense iron core stripped of everything useful; its magnetic scrape is logged as a nuisance in every navigation manual covering the inner system.

planets.name: Great Rose
planets.notes: Banded rose-and-ochre winds with a stable central storm; navigators sight on its petal patterns the way their ancestors sighted on compass roses drawn on paper.

planets.name: Colophon
planets.notes: The system's closing mark: a vast blue-slate giant whose skim yards service outbound convoys, stamped at the end of every shipping manifest filed here.

planets.name: Rimepage
planets.notes: A cracked ice shell over a briny mantle; robotic samplers drill it each summer of its long year, cataloguing organics nobody has funded a follow-up to study.

planets.name: Errata
planets.notes: A misprinted little world in a slightly wrong orbit; the Guild keeps it on the books purely so the charts stay honest about being wrong once.

planets.name: Pale Index
planets.notes: A dim, albedo-flat ice ball used as the outer alignment mark when calibrating long-baseline instruments aimed at the Lens.

planets.name: Final Leaf
planets.notes: The last turned page of the system; past it lies only the Lens and the dark the Lens looks into.

anomalies.name: Argus Lens
anomalies.notes: A vast natural gravitational lens that magnifies the deep field beyond the Shelf; the Deep Survey Guild built its flagship observatory along the focal line and restricts all approach corridors.

asteroid_belts.name: Countinghouse Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: A rich metallic swarm claimed jointly by the fisher-clans' trust and the Guild; its yield pays for the schools on Tideledger and the mirrors above it alike.

stations.name: Tideledger High Port
stations.notes: The colony's front door: fish processing, passenger halls, and the Almanac House where the tidal tables are sworn before publication.

stations.name: Colophon Yards
stations.notes: Fuel skimming and convoy assembly in the giant's shadow; outward-bound captains sign the yard's master ledger before departing the system.

stations.name: Focal Array One
stations.location: along the Lens focal line, beyond orbit 10
stations.notes: The Guild's crown jewel: a kilometer-wide mosaic of mirrors riding the focal line, returning charts of galaxies the naked eye will never see. Access by invitation, and lately by injunction.

faction_control.notes: The Guild administers the system under an old charter and guards Lens access jealously, but three consortia hold provisional observation berths won in court, and the fisher-clans' trust holds the belt like a purse string. Everyone is polite. Nobody is comfortable.

history: Charter was granted late in the expansion era to the fisher-clans of Tideledger, whose generational tidal records quietly became the sector's standard ephemeris.
Discovery of the Argus Lens transformed a quiet ocean backwater into the scientific prize of the Shelf, and the Deep Survey Guild relocated its entire Deep Field program here within a decade.
Arbitration over Lens access enters its sixth year, with the consortia pressing for permanent berths and the Guild arguing that some windows, once opened, cannot be shut again.
description: An old orange star counts out ten worlds in slow, even strokes, from the cinder called Kiln to the frozen footnote of Final Leaf. Between them run warm seas, rose-striped giants, and one dense glittering belt. The system reads like a well-kept account book, and its inhabitants rather like that.

Four hundred thousand people live on and above Tideledger, fishing, processing, and maintaining the almanacs that order shipping across the sector, while the Guild's nine hundred observers ride the focal line out beyond the last page. Moderate traffic flows through the High Port and the Colophon Yards, most of it honest, all of it recorded. What happens past Final Leaf is recorded too, but only by the Guild.

Everyone wants a look through the Lens. The consortia with provisional berths whisper about what the Guild's charts might show, and the Guild answers with injunctions, which convinces no one of nothing except that there is something worth seeing. On Tideledger, the almanac-keepers note a further unease: certain deep-field entries appear in the public summaries years late, if at all, and the tide tables have begun carrying corrections nobody remembers issuing.
